headline: AEI/VAT predictor schema audit; no ecological outcome inference.
2-km breeding-option atlas passed coverage and variation gate before demographic outcomes.
Tier-2 richness retained as primary heterogeneity trait; redundant alternatives demoted before outcomes.
Terrain atlas passed coverage; relief retained, absolute elevation kept contextual.
Palmer concentration occurred by dominance turnover whereas Signy retained and strengthened its initial core.
Five local trajectories all had positive abundance–E scaling; common descriptive kappa about 0.25.
Smooth scaling beat fixed hinges, annual first-difference coupling was weak, and no simple predictor explained kappa.
Apparent island morphology was largely compositional; within-Adelie island phenotype was weak and temporally reassembled.
Macro sample was broad but geographically uneven; species and geography partly confounded.
MAPPPD contained 152 Pygoscelis candidate site×species trend units and 92 stricter units.
Observation vantage/accuracy heterogeneity audited before demographic modeling.
All three stable-roster Palmer populations concentrated beyond proportional thinning under the full frozen count-error family.
Effective colony number showed a small positive next-year growth association beyond abundance and time; predictive framing was later downgraded.
Independent Torgersen mapping showed strong habitat-structured footprint loss, converging at phenomenon level but not identifier level.
Most observed variability reduction occurred within islands rather than among islands, but biological buffering was not yet identified.
Post-hoc diagnostics showed the hierarchy was not explained solely by comparing more lower-level units.
Raw hierarchy exceeded Poisson/CV10 expectations but was compatible with the uncalibrated CV20 sensitivity; strong buffering claim fails.
Fixed >50-pair group metrics improved prediction but coefficients reversed the preregistered protective direction.
Five Palmer islands shared a dominant long-term decline component (PC1 96.4%) while annual growth synchrony was only moderate.
Manuscript figure package reproduced frozen numerical results.
Public mark/resight sources lacked the band-to-later-breeding-site bridge required for direct retention/dispersal inference.
N_eff coefficient remained unusual under coupled circular-shift/count-error nulls; prediction remained unsupported.
Positive N_eff coefficient survived serial-structure-preserving circular-shift nulls, including exact covariance-preserving shifts.
N_eff association persisted after one- and two-year prior-growth controls, but incremental prediction became tiny.
Shared current-year count error did not generate an observed-scale positive N_eff coefficient under frozen sensitivities.
Held-out predictive gain was null-compatible (p=0.262) although the conditional coefficient remained unusual; prediction claim rejected.
Multi-island Adelie decline was estimable and replicated; synchronized multi-island composition reassembly was not estimable.
Reproductive performance showed weak 1–2 year memory and added information beyond current state, consistent with layered local dynamics.
Bias-resistant lag-2 performance→redistribution association survived fixed specification after provenance repair; not fully preregistered.
Species sorting plus year-specific within-species structure explained apparent island phenotype better than persistent island ecotypes.
Pooled colony-size/chick association was island-dependent; Palmer-wide Allee-like reproduction and pre-extinction collapse were not supported.
Preceding-year sea-ice duration and its habitat moderation failed the preregistered positive annual-growth mechanism.
Predeclared 3/5/7-year sea-ice-duration rescue failed; simple low-frequency duration did not explain the shared decline.
October snowfall×habitat interaction was opposite the preregistered direction and worsened held-out prediction.
Specific win-stay/lose-switch asymmetry failed; redistribution remained compatible with several broader dynamic processes.
All three simple area effects were negative but none survived preregistered species-specific Holm inference; buffering hypothesis unsupported.
Season field and 1980–2025 window fixed before count magnitudes were opened.
Synthetic recovery showed the cross-species median interaction estimand was recoverable before outcomes.
Observed non-confirmatory interaction does not exclude moderate effects, but common effects around |0.50–0.55| would usually have been detected.
First real-count V3 point estimates were explicitly non-inferential pending frozen permutation testing.
Regional versus species-wide forcing sensitivity was fixed before outcomes.
Forcing support/coverage passed outcome-blind eligibility rules for all three species.
Synthetic H-main recovery passed before real outcomes; terrain-R inference remained unopened.
Hierarchical estimator passed only under species-wide forcing; regional recovery failure constrained the final estimator before outcomes.
Initial integrated estimator failed synthetic recovery before any real demographic magnitude was opened; triggered redesign rather than threshold relaxation.
Exclude-unknown remained testable for all species; ground-only was coverage-limited for Adelie before outcomes.
Latent-factor scale recovery selected species-specific forcing scales before outcome access; observation layer still unopened.
Direct/image overlap and accuracy structure were audited outcome-blind to define the observation model.
Synthetic observation layer recovered the shared image offset and frozen accuracy structure before real outcomes.
Exact-date/≤14-day calibration changed offsets modestly but not the interaction direction; primary permutation result remained non-confirmatory.
A×H crossover design was full-rank/identifiable in all species before demographic outcomes.
Observed 2→5 km sign reversal was compatible with the joint radius null (p=0.081); biological scale-dependence claim prohibited.
A×H interaction was not invariant to radius or diversity metric; primary pattern cannot be a general island-architecture law.
Spatially adjusted species-wide V3 estimator passed all frozen synthetic recovery checks before real outcomes.
Common 1980–2025 trend endpoint availability was established without opening demographic values.
Outcome-blind source-sensitivity support rules identified testable lanes; Adelie ground-only was coverage-limited but nonblocking.
V2 exclude-unknown recovery missed the frozen 90/100 rule (88/100); no threshold relaxation and outcomes remained locked.
All three interaction estimates were negative, but the preregistered cross-species permutation test failed (p=0.0947); no Holm species rejection.
V3 source-robustness gate failed Adelie exclude-unknown recovery (86/100); no threshold was relaxed and outcomes stayed locked.
Paper-level cross-species source robustness passed before outcome unlock while Adelie-specific limitation remained explicit.
Prospectively frozen independent-system Adelie test replicated non-proportional concentration.
Separately frozen chinstrap test replicated concentration across species.
Post-result quality audit retained the frozen primary concentration result unchanged and forbade rescue exclusions.
Earlier/strict Signy Adelie concentration replication passed all frozen error models; same independence group as the later Signy Adelie record.
Palmer lag-2 performance-linked redistribution did not replicate under the frozen Signy primary design; transferability not established.
Outcome-blind Signy support audit passed feasibility for the later redistribution replication; effect not yet computed in this record.
